heroHeadline: Visayas Grid Hit With New Red Alert as Mindanao Normalizes; Tropical Depression 'Queenie' Nears PAR
heroSubtitle: The M7.8 Mindanao earthquake and tsunami, Typhoon Bavi's landslides, and the Luis-Maymay-Neneng-Dolphin-Kujira-Obet-Pilandok storm sequence have killed 173+ across the cascade; NDRRMC's storm-sequence toll still holds at 44 dead, 18 injured and 5 missing (last updated Sept 10), with DSWD's most recent count showing 46,424 evacuees in 570 centers as of Sept 13. The Visayas grid was hit with a fresh 1-hour red alert on Sept 22 after the Palinpinon-2 geothermal plant tripped, on top of an ongoing yellow alert from continued coal-unit outages, while the Mindanao grid returned to normal Sept 23 as GNPower Kauswagan and Therma South units resynchronized. Diesel's national average eased slightly to ₱102.78/liter by Sept 23 following Monday's third major fuel hike, still driven by Middle East conflict and drone-attack damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline. A tropical depression roughly 1,810km east of southeastern Luzon is forecast to enter the PAR Sept 24 as tropical storm 'Queenie' — the 17th cyclone of 2026 — with its trough already soaking Eastern Visayas, Caraga, Davao Oriental, Misamis Oriental and Camiguin. Separately, the GMA Kapuso Foundation delivered relief goods to over 9,000 earthquake and flood survivors across Sarangani's Glan, Maasim, Malapatan and Alabel.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
